explanation shown to learner: *I have no idea…* is a statement, not a question, so it ends with a full stop: *I have no idea why my phone keeps switching off.* Only a sentence that asks (*Could you tell me…?*, *Do you know…?*) has a question mark.
explanation in Latvian: Teikums par *phone* nav jautājums, tāpēc beigās ir punkts: … *why my phone keeps switching off*. Jautājuma zīme ir vajadzīga, kad teikums jautā: *Could you tell me*…?, *Do you know*…?

topic: Indirect questions (Could you tell me where...)
task: Which sentence has a mistake?
correct answer: I wonder how Anna's job interview went?
wrong options / checks: Could you tell me which room the exam is in? | I'm not sure how many people are coming. | Can you tell me how you made this soup?
explanation shown to learner: *I wonder…* is not a question, so it ends with a full stop: *I wonder how Anna's job interview went.* *Could you tell me…?* and *Can you tell me…?* are questions, so they keep the question mark.
explanation in Latvian: *I wonder*… nav jautājums, tāpēc beigās ir punkts: *I wonder how Anna's job interview went.* *Could you tell me*…? un *Can you tell me*…? ir jautājumi, tāpēc tiem ir jautājuma zīme.

topic: Indirect questions, more uses (I don't know what to do)
task: Which sentence means you give your manager an answer in either case?
correct answer: Tell your manager whether you can work on Saturday.
wrong options / checks: If you can work on Saturday, tell your manager. | If you can't work on Saturday, tell your manager. | Tell your manager that you can work on Saturday.
explanation shown to learner: *whether* = yes or no: you give your manager the answer in either case. *If* at the start is a condition: you tell your manager only in that one case. *that you can work* gives only one answer.
explanation in Latvian: *whether* nozīmē vai: vadītājam atbildi saki jebkurā gadījumā. *If* teikuma sākumā ir nosacījums (ja): saki to vienīgi tajā vienā gadījumā. *that you can work* dod vienu atbildi.

topic: Indirect questions, more uses (I don't know what to do)
task: Which sentence means you call the airline only when there is a problem?
correct answer: If your bag doesn't arrive, call the airline.
wrong options / checks: Call the airline to ask whether your bag has arrived. | Whether or not your bag arrives, call the airline. | Call the airline and ask if your bag has arrived.
explanation shown to learner: *If* + a condition at the start: you call only in that case. *ask whether* and *ask if* report a question, so you call anyway to get the answer; *whether or not* = in both cases.
explanation in Latvian: *If* teikuma sākumā ir nosacījums (ja): zvanīt vajag vienīgi tad. *ask whether* un *ask if* nozīmē pajautāt, vai, tāpēc zvanīt vajag jebkurā gadījumā; *whether or not* nozīmē jebkurā gadījumā.

topic: Indirect questions, more uses (I don't know what to do)
task: Which sentence has a mistake?
correct answer: We still haven't decided if to rent a car in Crete.
wrong options / checks: Everything now depends on whether the bank approves our loan. | If the train is delayed, I'll take a taxi. | Could you check whether the hotel has a lift?
explanation shown to learner: Before *to* + verb only *whether* is possible: *We still haven't decided whether to rent a car*. *If* needs a subject and a verb: *if we should rent a car*.
explanation in Latvian: Pirms to + darbības vārds var būt *tikai whether*: *We still haven't decided whether to rent a car.* Aiz *if* vajag teikuma priekšmetu un darbības vārdu: *if we should rent a car*.

topic: Indirect questions, more uses (I don't know what to do)
task: The hotel wants to know ___ to expect us before ten, and ___ we're late, they'll keep the room for us until midnight.
correct answer: whether / if
explanation shown to learner: Before *to* + verb only *whether* is possible: *whether to expect us*. *if we're late* is a condition: they keep the room for us only in that case.
explanation in Latvian: Saka *whether to expect us*, nevis *if to expect us*. *if we're late* ir nosacījums (ja): viesnīca gaidīs vienīgi tad.

topic: Indirect questions, more uses (I don't know what to do)
task: Complete with one word: The caterer needs to know ___ or not you're coming to the wedding.
correct answer: whether
explanation shown to learner: Directly before *or not* only *whether* is possible: *whether or not you're coming*. *if or not* is a mistake.
explanation in Latvian: Tieši pirms *or not* var būt vienīgi *whether*: *whether or not you're coming*. *if or not* ir kļūda.
